sentence: An entrepreneur can engage a self‑employed business owner as a contractor, since self‑employed individuals are able to contract out their services to others while maintaining their own company.
The self‑employed is described as someone who essentially owns a job and can be hired by another firm, distinct from a business owner who runs a separate enterprise.
Investors may buy a 0% yield bond because they value the certainty of receiving the full principal back on a known date, even though the bond provides no positive return.

Even with no yield, the security of a government‑backed bond can be worth the small “cost” of holding cash that otherwise incurs storage and security expenses, making it attractive for risk‑averse investors.
If market participants expect overall yields to move further negative, the price of a zero‑yield bond could rise, allowing the holder to sell later at a profit despite the current zero return.
The fact that a large portion of the world’s bond market now contains negative‑yielding securities demonstrates that investors do find rational reasons to hold bonds that offer no positive yield.
Education loans are treated as standard loans that often require the item being financed as collateral, and lenders usually ask for documentation such as a payslip to verify repayment ability.
If a borrower cannot provide the required collateral or proof of income, the bank may consider the applicant ineligible and reject the loan.
Consequently, not having a payslip that can serve as collateral can result in the education loan application being denied.
If you withdraw the CD before its one‑year maturity, you will incur an early‑withdrawal penalty, such as the three‑month penalty described for early pulls.
Because of that penalty, it may be better to move the funds to a liquid savings account, which offers a comparable rate without the access restriction.
For future deposits, consider using a CD ladder, which staggers maturities every few months so you have periodic access to portions of your money.
If you anticipate needing the money soon, keep that portion in a standard savings account rather than locking it in a CD, as the savings account provides immediate access.
In double‑entry bookkeeping every transaction is recorded as a debit to one account and a credit to another, with the total debits equaling the total credits.
The terms debit and credit describe the operation performed on an account, not the type of account itself, so the same account can be debited at one time and credited at another.
Assets are debit accounts, meaning a debit increases an asset balance, while liabilities are credit accounts, meaning a credit increases a liability balance.
When an account’s balance is positive it is said to be “in credit”, and when it shows a net amount owed it is “in debit” according to standard dictionary definitions.
The borrower remains liable for the full amount of the loan even after the property is foreclosed and sold.
If the foreclosure sale does not cover the outstanding principal, interest, and fees, the remaining deficiency is still the ex‑homeowner’s responsibility.
Only a bankruptcy filing can potentially eliminate that deficiency, but otherwise the debt persists.
In some cases a lender may choose to forgive the deficiency, which would then be treated as taxable income.
Opening a US bank account without being physically present is difficult.
Some banks do permit online account opening that can be managed remotely once set up.
Your bank will focus on your tax status, and as a US tax resident you will need to open a US‑resident account and be subject to US tax rules.
You will also be required to file US tax returns on the income in the account, and may face double taxation unless a treaty applies.
You should create a separate QuickBooks company file for each LLC that holds a property, treating each as its own entity in the system.
Keep separate checking accounts, credit cards, and other finances for each LLC, opening them with the LLC’s EIN to preserve the legal protection of the entity.
If you want the parent rental company to reflect ownership of the LLCs, record the subsidiary LLCs as assets on the parent’s books, but be aware this adds overhead and cost.
Set up a distinct bank account for each LLC and pay yourself from that account based on hours or income, which helps keep expenses and income separate for tax purposes.
Never mix personal and company assets and maintain proper records to maintain liability protection and any tax benefits.
The monthly payment can be expressed with the standard loan‑payment formula M = P × [J / (1 − (1 + J)^‑N)], where P is the principal, J the monthly interest rate and N the number of months.

When returns are reinvested, the cash‑flow stream is treated as an annuity and the money‑weighted return equation is solved numerically to obtain the monthly rate, which is then converted to a nominal annual rate compounded monthly.
The required number of periods N can be determined with the NPER function or the derived formula for payments, as shown in the loan‑payment discussion.
The present value of the reinvested returns can be calculated in Excel using the PV function with the appropriate monthly rate and period count.
Applying the solved rate to the annuity formula therefore yields the monthly payment received at any time t.
If an employer incorrectly classifies a worker as an independent contractor, the IRS can reclassify the worker as an employee, making the employer liable for the employment taxes that were not paid.
The employer may also face penalties and lose any relief provisions that would have applied to a proper classification.
For the employee, reclassification can mean that the employer must withhold and pay the employer’s share of FICA taxes, which the employee would otherwise have to cover themselves as a contractor.
Additionally, the employee may lose benefits associated with employee status and could be subject to an audit or additional tax liability if the employer’s reclassification was improper.
Income from YouTube or Twitch is treated as earnings and is only taxable if it exceeds the costs of producing the content.
Allowable expenses include items such as the purchase price of a computer, video camera, and the cost of broadband connection.
If the revenue from the videos does not surpass these expenses, no tax is due.
Hemp is currently an easy crop to grow but yields lower value than major crops such as canola, oats, or soybeans, and acreage in Canada has been declining due to cost and weak demand.
The primary motivation for Canadian farmers to plant hemp is crop rotation rather than high profitability, indicating limited immediate financial upside.
While legalization of cannabis could change supply and demand dynamics, the impact on hemp distribution channels is uncertain and may not translate into strong investment returns.
Moreover, the author of the evidence does not believe that legalizing cannabis will create a great investing opportunity for existing hemp producers, suggesting caution for investors.
Equity should be divided according to how much each person actually paid into the mortgage and related expenses, so the split reflects each party’s financial contribution.
A formal written partnership agreement prepared by a lawyer should spell out each partner’s ownership share, responsibilities, and an exit strategy to protect both parties.

If you cannot obtain a joint mortgage, the bank will hold only the borrower personally liable, and any side agreement giving the partner a claim to equity does not give them direct rights against the lender.

Using a joint account to track all mortgage payments allows you to reimburse each person’s initial contributions and then split any remaining proceeds 50‑50, or adjust the split based on who paid more toward the mortgage.
Finally, working with a financial professional to set up proper accounting and tax treatment will help you run the property ownership like a simple business and avoid complications later.
An LLC, whether a sole‑proprietor, partnership, corporation or LLC, is eligible to establish a SEP‑IRA.
The SEP contribution may be up to 25 % of compensation, but for self‑employed LLC owners the limit is 20 % of compensation with an overall dollar cap (e.g., $49,000 in 2011 or $50,000 in 2012).

When the LLC owner is self‑employed, the contribution is calculated on business income after subtracting half of the self‑employment tax, limited to 20 % of that income and subject to a maximum (e.g., $45,000 in earlier years).

SEP contributions count toward the aggregate defined‑contribution limit, which is the lesser of $53,000 (or the 2024 equivalent) or 100 % of the participant’s compensation, and must be added to contributions made to any other defined‑contribution plans the LLC maintains.
You may maintain both a SEP‑IRA and other retirement plans, but you must have sufficient business income to fund the SEP contribution.
Warren Buffett and Charlie Munger stress that the only thing they read is financial statements, which is essential for a buy‑and‑hold approach suited to long‑term small investors.

They recommend that small investors keep the portfolio simple by placing about 10 % of cash in short‑term government bonds and the remaining 90 % in a very low‑cost S&P 500 index fund, such as Vanguard’s.
Reading Buffett’s annual letters to shareholders is also advised, as it teaches how to think about businesses beyond financial modelling.
For further guidance, studying Buffett’s collected essays provides insight into how companies generate value and his overall investment philosophy, which is valuable for individual investors.
VAT is charged by the seller only if they are VAT‑registered, and the buyer’s status does not affect whether VAT is collected.
If the seller failed to include VAT on the invoice, the tax was never collected and there is no amount owed to the seller for that VAT.
VAT must be paid to the tax authority, not to the supplier, so you are not required to pay the company for VAT they did not charge.
If you have paid interest on qualified student loans, you can deduct up to $2,500 as an adjustment to income provided your MAGI is below $60,000 and you are not filing Married Filing Separately.

To claim education credits for qualified tuition and related expenses, the expenses must be paid by you, your spouse, or a dependent; payments made directly to the school by a third party are treated as if you paid them, but you cannot claim expenses for someone else unless they qualify as your dependent.
Even if you are not required to file based on income, filing a return can allow you to receive a refund of any withheld tax and to claim student tax credits that may result in a refund.
Be sure to file Form 1040 by the annual deadline (typically April 15, with extensions as announced) and consider using the IRS Free File program if your income is low.
Many banks’ online bill‑pay services let you send payments to any company or person, and will mail a paper check if the recipient cannot accept electronic funds.
Bill‑pay is typically funded from a checking account, which most banks support for these transactions.
Thus you can use the bill‑pay feature of your online checking account to pay taxes, as the tax authority can receive either an electronic transfer or a mailed check.
